title: Telescopes
examples: What is the difference between a refracting and reflecting telescope?
Why are space telescopes better than ground telescopes?
Can you show me a picture of the Hubble Space Telescope?

explain.say: Today we will learn about telescopes used to see space.
Some telescopes use lenses to bend the light they collect.
Other telescopes use curved mirrors to gather and focus the light.
Space telescopes look above Earth's atmosphere for clearer views.
The Hubble Space Telescope orbits Earth to avoid atmospheric distortion.
A real-life example is looking at planets like Jupiter.

faq.q: Why can't we just use bigger ground telescopes?
faq.a: Earth's atmosphere wobbles and blurs the light from space. Space telescopes escape this blurring effect entirely. It is also called atmospheric distortion.
asks: Does the air mess up telescope pictures?
Why is space better than ground for seeing stars?

faq.q: What is the main difference between lenses and mirrors in telescopes?
faq.a: Lenses bend light using curved glass, while mirrors bend light using polished, curved surfaces. Both aim to focus distant light sources. They are two different ways to achieve the same goal.
asks: Which is better, glass or metal for telescopes?
How do lenses and mirrors work together?

asks: Must all big telescopes be in space?
Are there any space telescopes that are not Hubble?

faq.a: It is the bending of light as it passes through layers of air with different temperatures. This makes stars and galaxies look wavy or fuzzy through ground telescopes. Space telescopes avoid this problem.
asks: What is the problem with viewing from the ground?
Can the air make stars look weird?

faq.q: Do refracting telescopes have any weaknesses?
faq.a: Yes, large lenses can suffer from chromatic aberration, which splits light into colors. This is a major reason why reflecting telescopes are often used instead. Mirrors do not have this color splitting issue.
asks: What color problems do lenses cause?
Why do lenses sometimes look rainbowy?

facts: Refracting telescopes use lenses to gather light.
Reflecting telescopes use mirrors to gather light.
Space telescopes avoid Earth's atmosphere for clearer views.
The Hubble Space Telescope is a famous example of a space telescope.

quiz.say: Which type of telescope uses curved mirrors to focus light?
quiz.why: Reflecting telescopes are designed specifically to use mirrors to collect and focus light from space.

wrong.0: Refracting telescopes use lenses, not mirrors, to bend the light.
wrong.1: Atmospheric is a condition, not a type of telescope.
wrong.2: Orbital describes where it is, not how it focuses light.

quiz.say: Why are space telescopes better than ground telescopes?
quiz.why: The primary advantage of space telescopes is that they are above the Earth's atmosphere, which causes blurring.

wrong.0: Size is not the main reason; the location is more important.
wrong.1: While some can, the main advantage is clarity, not just wavelength.
wrong.2: Space missions are extremely complex and very expensive.

quiz.say: If a telescope uses glass lenses, what type is it?
quiz.why: The use of lenses to bend light is the defining characteristic of a refracting telescope.

wrong.0: Space describes the location, not the optical mechanism.
wrong.1: This term describes the environment, not the instrument type.
wrong.3: Reflecting telescopes use mirrors, not lenses.
